lead.headline: Mahomes Throws Five, Chiefs Roll in Atlanta
lead.subhead: Patrick Mahomes threw five touchdown passes and Kansas City beat the Falcons 35-13 on the road. Elsewhere Sunday, Kirk Cousins won his first game back in purple as Minnesota beat Green Bay 30-10 at Lambeau, and Detroit handled New England 35-10 in Munich. The best keep stacking reps until the scoreboard has no choice.

articles.hed: Harrison Wins 10 Months After Neck Surgery
articles.body: Ten months after neck and spinal surgery, Kayla Harrison submitted Amanda Nunes in the fourth round at Madison Square Garden to keep her bantamweight title. She's now 20-1 as a pro. Fall down, get rebuilt, stand back up and win the biggest fight of your life.

Darius Fulghum pressured the previously unbeaten Diego Pacheco from the opening bell in Carson, California, won the battle of the jabs and took the decision 115-112, 115-112, 114-113. The challenger who shows up hungrier writes the headline.

openingBell.title: The Opening Bell
openingBell.intro: Monday, the day of the Moon. Four counts in, four hold, four out, four hold. The Moon is the old symbol of rhythm: it never skips a phase. Breathe square, find your rhythm, and set the week's pace before anyone else does.

breathing.title: Box Breathing — 4 · 4 · 4 · 4

phases.label: INHALE
phases.cue: Draw in through the nose — even, quiet, full.

phases.label: HOLD
phases.cue: Stillness at the top. No strain. Own the pause.

phases.label: HOLD
phases.cue: Empty and steady. Reset the line.

breathing.close: Four rounds squares the mind. Eyes open. Shoulders down. Body next. Then go build.

mindset.body: The Bulls' flight got grounded. They landed on game day, missing three players, and still beat a team on a five-game heater. Conditions are never perfect: the pipeline is thin, the week is long, the market is noisy. Winners play anyway and play harder. Plan the week today like you're already ahead of it. Competitive. Unbeatable. Always rising. fall down 7 stand up 8.

bodyOpener.title: 3-Minute Opener
bodyOpener.note: Monday, the day of the Moon: run this right after Morning Charge. It's about 27° and clear outside, so keep the RipStick finisher indoors. First rep of the week sets the tone.

moves.name: Push-ups
moves.body: Crisp reps, chest to floor. If you hit 30 early, hold high plank until the minute mark.

moves.name: Plank
moves.body: Elbows or hands. Ribs down, glutes on. Breathe slow.

moves.name: RipStick finisher
moves.body: Dom's RipStick (RipRight): hold sticks at chest → inhale and pull apart as wide as possible → with bands open, exhale and push arms straight out while keeping them apart (dynamic isometrics / Push-Pulls). Smooth continuous reps for the remaining time.

items.body: Kayla Harrison choked out Amanda Nunes in the fourth at UFC 334, and Ciryl Gane beat Josh Hokit by decision in a fight with a record 383 significant strikes for a UFC heavyweight bout.
Darius Fulghum took the WBC Silver and WBO International belts on a decision in Carson. Anthony Olascuaga also retained his WBO flyweight title over Yuberjen Martinez.
Round-by-round breakdown of Gane-Hokit and Harrison-Nunes from Madison Square Garden.

items.hed: The Moon and the soul's tides
items.body: Monday belongs to the Moon. Hermetic and astrological writers made the Moon the sphere nearest Earth, ruling rhythm, memory and the tides. The lesson: master your cycles and you stop being pushed around by them.

The 14th-century German mystic taught that beneath every passing mood sits a still ground where the soul and the divine meet. Work from that ground and the noise of the day can't knock you off your center.

In the Gnostic text Pistis Sophia, Sophia falls into the lower realms and sings repentances until she's lifted back up, step by step. It's one of the oldest fall-and-rise stories there is: the climb back is made of repeated effort.

lesson.oneLiner: A resource list is only worth something when you ship one thing with it.
beats: Open the thread and pick the single resource closest to what you're building now, like a 7EightMade landing page.
Scroll-driven and 3D effects look great, but they cost load time. Use one per page, as the hero moment, not everywhere.
Copy the prompt or source, swap in your own brand colors and copy, and test it on your phone first.
Keep what works in a small personal snippets folder so the next drop page starts halfway done.
lesson.takeaway: Save less, ship more: one resource, one page, this week.
